title: Naked Happy Girls

description.main: Andrew Einhorn's Naked Happy Girls, published by Goliath in 2003, is a 368-page book of nudes photographed in the subjects' own New York apartments, women he approached on the street, with a short text on each, and pictures that first ran on his Manhattan public-access show Dog the Cat.
description.extended:
Andrew Einhorn's Naked Happy Girls, published by Goliath in 2003, is a book of nudes photographed in the subjects' own New York apartments, a photojournalist's take on the girl-next-door genre that grew out of a Manhattan public-access cable show.

Einhorn approached women on the street and asked them to pose at home. The 368 pages are divided into short sections, one per model, each opened by a paragraph of his own text, after a one-page introduction by Emma Jane Taylor. The pictures are unretouched and keep the rooms, books and clutter of each apartment in the frame; the cover shows a model turning a movie camera back on the photographer. Goliath issued it in its small oblong hardcover format, and the same ISBN was later reused for a 2015 softcover reprint.

Einhorn was born in Philadelphia in 1964, studied journalism at Temple University and spent five years as a photojournalist at the Philadelphia Inquirer before moving to New York in 1994. The nude portraits of friends and strangers he began making there fed Dog the Cat, the cable show he produced for seven years, and this book collects them. Goliath followed with Bubble Bath Girls (2005) and Naked Coast to Coast.
description.artist_bio: Andrew Einhorn (b. 1964, Philadelphia) studied journalism at Temple University, worked five years as a photojournalist at the Philadelphia Inquirer, and moved to New York in 1994, where he produced the public-access show Dog the Cat for seven years and works as a photographer, videographer, editor and comedian. Goliath published Naked Happy Girls (2003), Bubble Bath Girls (2005) and Naked Coast to Coast.
